main_body: A side-facing wooden chair (west-facing): a tall backrest on the right with an L-shaped profile, and a seat slab running left, with dark legs below.
top_band: A light tan band at rows ~11-12 forms the seat edge, only about 2px tall, and it is the same tone as the front of the seat. The rows above it are the backrest's side profile. No real horizontal seat surface is seen from above.
evidence: The chair is a side profile: the backrest is a tall vertical column and the seat reads as a thin L-shaped arm with only a 1-2px light edge on top. Legs are dark stubs below. It matches the guide's red 'side elevation chair' and 'thin seat' cases, because there is no seat surface of several rows visible from above, and no front-edge line or eave shadow under it.

style.evidence: Wood has about 3 tones (light tan, mid orange-brown, dark brown) with a dark brown outline tinted to the material, which is fine. However the backrest and seat are large flat fills with no grain or texture dots, and the small tiles carry only 3-4 colours each. This is much thinner than the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and rich texture.
